lesson.grammar_point: adverbs of frequency with the present simple (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) and how often

listenings.text: Hi, I'm Jack, and I live outside Sydney. My commute is long: about an hour and a half every morning. I usually take the train at six thirty. I never drive to work, because at rush hour the traffic jams are terrible. On the train I always listen to a podcast. One episode is about forty minutes, so I finish one on the way to work and one on the way home. Sometimes I read a book. I work from home twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. On those days I sleep a little more, and I never run late.

Hello, my name is Priya, and I'm an HR analyst in London. Two years ago I took the bus to work, but I often got stuck in traffic, and I was always late. Now I commute by bike. It takes twenty-five minutes, and I know a shortcut through a park. I never get stuck, and I usually arrive at the office before my boss. When it rains a lot, I take the subway. In the evening, I sometimes ride home with a colleague from the finance department. We talk about work on the way, so when we arrive home, work is finished.
